title: Aleph Farms of Rehovot grew a steak from the cells of Lucy the cow and received approval to sell it in Israel

trailer.text: Aleph Farms is an Israeli food-tech company from Rehovot, founded in 2017 by Didier Toubia, Dr. Neta Lavon and Prof. Shulamit Levenberg of the Technion.
The company grows steak from the cells of a Black Angus cow named Lucy.
The cells grow in tanks that act as fermenters, similar to the tanks in a brewery.
In January 2024, the Times of Israel reported that, according to the Health Ministry, Israel became the first in the world to approve the sale of cultured meat based on beef.
According to Green Queen, in 2026 the company also received approval from the Singapore Food Agency.

glance.label: Founders
glance.value: Didier Toubia, Dr. Neta Lavon, Prof. Shulamit Levenberg

glance.label: Source of the cells
glance.value: A Black Angus cow named Lucy

paragraphs.text: Didier Toubia, CEO of Aleph Farms, explained that he chose beef because, in terms of land, water and greenhouse gas emissions, beef is the issue that needs to be addressed.
According to Calcalist, meat production is estimated to be responsible for about 16.5% of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.
According to vegconomist, the beef industry causes significant environmental damage, among other things through the release of methane.
Toubia told Globes that cultured meat can grow regardless of the amount of water or fertile land in the country.
Therefore, he said, it is very suitable for the Middle East.
He also said that jointly addressing food security is the good way to ensure prosperity in the Middle East and in regions that depend on food imports, mainly in Asia.

stations.title: A Technion lab, an incubator and three founders

paragraphs.text: According to Globes, Aleph Farms was founded based on the research of Prof. Shulamit Levenberg of the Technion.
According to Ynetnews, the company was founded in 2017 by Didier Toubia, Dr. Neta Lavon and Prof. Levenberg.
According to the Times of Israel, the Strauss Group's food-tech incubator The Kitchen was a partner in the founding.
Toubia manages the company as CEO.
According to Ynetnews, in 2018 the company presented the world's first cultured beef steak.
In 2021, according to the same report, it presented the world's first cultured entrecote steak.

stations.title: How to grow a steak without slaughter

paragraphs.text: According to the company, the steak is made from the cells of a Black Angus cow named Lucy.
According to the company, apart from cells derived from one of Lucy's fertilized eggs, there are no animal-derived components in the production process or in the final product.
According to ynet, the cells did not undergo genetic modification or immortalization.
The tissue grows in tanks that act as fermenters, as in a brewery.
According to Neta Lavon, in 2021 the company moved to a growth medium without animal components.
According to AgFunderNews, the product was developed without fetal bovine serum, whose use is controversial.
According to the company, no antibiotics are used in production.

According to a Ministry of Health guideline, the product that the applicants chose to call "a thin cut from bovine cell culture" is a new food product containing a plant component derived from soy together with cells derived from cattle, grown under cell culture conditions.
According to Globes, beef makes up only about 20% of the first product, and the texture also comes from soy and wheat.
Toubia told Globes that the product is unique among the approved products, because it is a beef product with the texture of a steak, made from cells that were not genetically modified.
According to the Health Ministry, the Novel Food Committee decided on 6.12.2023 to recommend approving the registration of the novel food.
According to the company's statement, in December the ministry issued it a "no questions" letter for the Aleph Cuts brand, meaning the product is recognized as safe.
According to the ministry, the approval was granted in a joint pilot with the Innovation Authority that examines alternative proteins.
Dr. Ziva Hamama, head of the Food Risk Management Department, described what was examined: toxicology, allergenicity, nutritional composition, and microbiological and chemical safety.
According to the Health Ministry, the product is approved for marketing in a portion of up to 300 grams per day.
The product is not approved for marketing in other food categories.
According to the Times of Israel, Singapore and the United States had previously approved cultured chicken, and Israel is the first to approve beef.
According to AgFunderNews, the pre-approval the company received is the first-ever approval for a cultivated meat product that is not chicken.
According to the same report, it is also the first approval for a cultured meat company in the Middle East.
According to ynet, before writing his opinion, Chief Rabbi David Lau visited the plant in Rehovot and examined the production processes up close.
According to the Times of Israel, the ruling was based primarily on the fact that the meat is grown from stem cells from a fertilized egg, not from muscle tissue cells.
Rabbi Lau also noted a reservation.

According to Rabbi Lau, if cultivated meat is marketed as meat or as meat products, and particularly if it resembles meat in its taste and smell, there is reason to be stringent and to define it as kosher but not as pareve with regard to mixing it with dairy products.

However, according to him, if the cultivated meat is marketed as meat or resembles meat in its taste and smell, there is room to be stringent and define it as kosher but not as pareve with regard to mixing it, cooking it and eating it with dairy products, although the main point of his ruling was that the meat is "kosher pareve".
According to ynet, a position paper by the Tzohar rabbinical organization determined that cultured meat produced from cells in a laboratory is not meat (besari).
ynet asked whether a kosher restaurant could serve it with dairy products, that is, a kosher cheeseburger.
According to vegconomist, the company is also working to obtain Halal certification.

stations.title: What was said when it happened

paragraphs.text: Dr. Ziva Hamama said the approval makes Israel the first country in the world to approve bovine cell culture as food.
According to her, Israel is becoming a world leader in the field.
Ronit Eshel of the Innovation Authority said it was a historic day and that the Authority is proud to be part of the success.
Ella Waldman-Renzer of GFI Israel said the approval is a turning point for the Israeli and global food system.
Bruce Friedrich of the Good Food Institute said he is thrilled that consumers in Israel will soon be able to buy the products, as in the U.S. and Singapore.
Yifat Gavriel, the company's head of regulatory affairs, said 2024 could be a landmark year for cultured meat.
Toubia himself wrote on LinkedIn that some team members and their family members are directly involved in the war.
Therefore, he wrote, it is not appropriate to celebrate.
According to Globes, the investors included Peregrine Ventures, Strauss, Millennium Food Tech and the Singaporean VisVires fund.
According to Ynetnews, Cargill and the actor Leonardo DiCaprio also invested.
According to GFI Israel, in 2022, 454 million dollars were invested in Israeli companies in the alternative protein field, about 15% of investments worldwide.
According to Globes, in the first stage the company will sell to a small number of restaurants, at prices similar to premium steaks.
Yoav Reisler of the company said Aleph Cuts will be priced at launch like regular premium beef.
Toubia said the company works quite a bit with the UAE, and that the work has not been harmed because of the war.
According to TechCrunch, on July 26, 2023 the company submitted an application for approval in Switzerland.
According to Green Queen, approval from Singapore came nearly four years after the application was filed.
Toubia said the production line in Singapore is expected to be operational in the first half of 2027, with a launch in select restaurants.
According to Ynetnews, cultured meat producers face two major challenges: the scale of production and the price.
According to Globes, Aleph Farms' production costs are very high, and the company does not expect to be profitable soon.
In July 2023, Calcalist cited an estimate according to which producing cultured meat costs roughly 180 to 900 dollars per kilogram.
According to Calcalist, cultured meat usually does not reach half of the final product.
Ronit Eshel told Calcalist that for at least the coming decade it will not be possible to eat a cut that is 100% cultured meat.
According to the Times of Israel, after the approval the company still had to go through a bureaucratic process before the products would reach buyers.
According to AgFunderNews, the company is cleared to sell in Israel, but is prioritizing other markets.
Israel Hayom noted that Italy has banned the use of cultured food.
According to Green Queen, the shift to an "asset-light" strategy led to several rounds of layoffs.
According to AgFunderNews, Toubia confirmed that the company laid off employees following a plan to shift production in Israel from the pilot facility to third parties.
According to Gavriel, the company moved to outsourced manufacturing, so the GMP requirements will apply to the partner site.
According to Toubia, an independent techno-economic analysis projects a production cost of $6.45 per pound and a 47% gross margin, at a price identical to conventional beef.

claims.quote: We’re thrilled that consumers in Israel will soon be able, like those in the U.S. and Singapore, to purchase these delicious products.

claims.text: יפעת גבריאל, ראשת הרגולציה באלף פארמס, אמרה ש-2024 עשויה להיות שנת ציון דרך בהסדרה ובמסחור של בשר מתורבת.
claims.quote: Yifat Gavriel, chief of regulatory affairs, quality assurance, and product safety at Aleph Farms, said 2024 could be a landmark year in regulating and commercializing cultivated meat.

claims.text: טוביה כתב בלינקדאין שחלק מחברי הצוות ובני משפחותיהם מעורבים ישירות במלחמה, ולכן לא ראוי לחגוג.
claims.quote: Some people on our team and their family members are directly involved, including by risking their lives fighting for freedom and democracy.

claims.text: לפי Globes (ינואר 2024), החברה הוקמה בחממת הפוד-טק The Kitchen וגייסה 140 מיליון דולר, בין היתר מ-Peregrine Ventures, שטראוס, מילניום פוד טק וקרן VisVires הסינגפורית.
claims.quote: The company was founded in The Kitchen food-tech incubator and has raised $140 millionm from Peregrine Ventures, Strauss, Millennium Food Tech (TASE: MIFT), Singapore's VisVires New Protein Fund

claims.text: לפי Ynetnews, מאז הקמתה גייסה החברה כ-140 מיליון דולר, בין היתר מ-Cargill ומליאונרדו דיקפריו.
claims.quote: Since it was established, the company has raised about 140 million dollars, with the notary funders being international food giant Cargill and Leonardo DiCaprio

claims.text: לפי GFI ישראל, ב-2022 הושקעו 454 מיליון דולר בחברות ישראליות בתחום, כ-15 אחוז מההשקעות העולמיות.
claims.quote: $454 million were invested in Israeli companies in the field which make up 15 percent of global investments in 2022

claims.text: לפי Globes, בשלב הראשון תמכור החברה למספר קטן של מסעדות במחירים הדומים לסטייקים פרימיום, לדברי המנכ"ל טוביה.
claims.quote: In the first stage, the company will sell only to a small number of restaurants to prices similar to prime cut premium steaks says Aleph Farms CEO Didier Toubia.

claims.text: יואב רייזלר מאלף פארמס אמר כי בהשקה הראשונית Aleph Cuts יתומחר בדומה לבקר קונבנציונלי פרימיום.
claims.quote: At the time of our soft launch, Aleph Cuts will be priced similarly to premium conventional beef

claims.text: טוביה אמר ל-Globes שהחברה עובדת לא מעט עם איחוד האמירויות ושהעבודה הזו לא נפגעה בגלל המלחמה.
claims.quote: We work quite a bit with the UAE, and this work has not been harmed as a result of the war.

claims.text: לפי TechCrunch, אלף פארמס הגישה בקשה לאישור בשוויץ ב-26 ביולי 2023.
claims.quote: This followed Aleph’s application submitted July 26 for regulatory approval in Switzerland.

claims.text: טוביה אמר ל-Green Queen שקו הייצור בסינגפור אמור לפעול בחציון הראשון של 2027, עם השקה אצל מסעדות נבחרות.
claims.quote: We are targeting our Singapore production line to be operational in the first half of 2027, launching with select restaurant partners

claims.text: לפי Ynetnews, יצרניות הבשר המתורבת ניצבות בפני שני אתגרים משמעותיים: היקף הייצור והתמחור.
claims.quote: the producers in the field face two significant challenges: the scale of production, which needs to be on a satisfactory scale to be a real alternative to animal-based meat

claims.text: לפי Globes, עלויות הייצור גבוהות מאוד והחברה אינה צופה להיות רווחית בקרוב.
claims.quote: Even so, the production costs are very high, and the company does not expect to be profitable anytime soon.

claims.text: כלכליסט ציין ביולי 2023 כי לפי הערכה אחת בשר מתורבת עולה בערך 180 עד 900 דולר לקילוגרם לייצור.
claims.quote: לפי הערכה אחת, בשר מתורבת עולה בערך 180 עד 900 דולר לקילוגרם לייצור

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, הבשר המתורבת במוצר הסופי לא מגיע לרוב למחצית כמות החומר.
claims.quote: הבשר המתורבת במוצר הסופי לא מגיע לרוב למחצית כמות החומר

claims.text: רונית אשל מרשות החדשנות אמרה לכלכליסט שבעשור הקרוב לפחות לא ניתן יהיה לצרוך נתח שהוא 100% בשר מתורבת.
claims.quote: בעשור הקרוב לפחות לא נוכל לצרוך נתח שהוא 100% בשר מתורבת

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, החברה עדיין צריכה לעבור הליך בירוקרטי לפני שהמוצרים יהיו זמינים לרכישה.
claims.quote: The company still faces a bureaucratic process before the products are available for purchase.

claims.text: לפי AgFunderNews (2026), אלף פארמס מורשית למכור סטייקים בישראל מאז 2023 אך נותנת עדיפות לשווקים אחרים.
claims.quote: While Aleph Farms has been cleared to sell its steaks in Israel since 2023, it is prioritizing other markets first, said Toubia.

claims.text: ישראל היום ציין שבעבר פרסם שאיטליה אסרה שימוש במזון מתורבת.
claims.quote: לא מכבר פרסמנו כאן ב"ישראל היום" כי איטליה אסרה שימוש במזון מתורבת

claims.text: לפי Green Queen, המעבר לאסטרטגיה קלת נכסים הוביל לכמה סבבי פיטורים.
claims.quote: The shift to an asset-light strategy has, however, led to multiple rounds of layoffs, including one earlier this year.

claims.text: לפי AgFunderNews, אלף פארמס פיטרה לאחרונה חברי צוות בעקבות תוכנית להעביר ייצור בישראל ממתקן הפיילוט לצדדים שלישיים, כך אישר טוביה.
claims.quote: Aleph has recently laid off some team members following plans to shift production in Israel from its pilot facility to third parties, he confirmed.

claims.text: לפי גבריאל, אלף פארמס עברה למודל ייצור במיקור חוץ, כך שדרישות ה-GMP יחולו על אתר השותף.
claims.quote: We have since moved to an outsourced manufacturing model, so the same GMP standards and regulatory expectations will apply to the partner site instead.

claims.text: לפי טוביה, ניתוח טכנו-כלכלי עצמאי מצביע על שולי רווח גולמי של 47% בשוויון מחירים עם בקר רגיל ועל עלות ייצור של 6.45 דולר לפאונד.
claims.quote: This projects a 47% gross margin at price parity with conventional beef, a unit production cost of $6.45 per pound, and a payback period in 2.5 years.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, הסטארט-אפ גייס עד אז כ-120 מיליון דולר ממשקיעים פרטיים וציבוריים, בהם השחקן ליאונרדו דיקפריו.
claims.quote: To date, the startup has raised a total of about $120 million from a number of private and public investors such as actor and environmental activist Leonardo DiCaprio.

claims.text: לפי Green Queen, החברה גייסה עד כה 147 מיליון דולר ומפעילה מפעל ברחובות בקיבולת ראשונית של 10 טון סטייק מתורבת בשנה.
claims.quote: The startup, which has raised $147M to date, operates a 65,000 sq ft plant in Rehovot, with a capacity to initially produce 10 tonnes of cultivated steak annually.

claims.text: לפי Green Queen, אישור סינגפור בא אחרי האישור לבקר המתורבת במדינת הבית בדצמבר 2023.
claims.quote: It follows the December 2023 clearance for the cultivated beef in its home country

claims.text: יפעת גבריאל מאלף פארמס אמרה שהאישור מותנה בהנחיות סימון ושיווק של משרד הבריאות ובהשלמת בדיקת GMP למתקן הייצור הפיילוט.
claims.quote: subject to specific directions for labeling and marketing provided by the Israeli Ministry of Health and the completion of a Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) inspection for our pilot production facility

claims.text: לפי Globes, אלף פארמס עדיין נדרשת לאישור לקו הייצור שלה, וההליכים צפויים להסתיים בחודשים הקרובים כך שהמוצרים יהיו זמינים עד אמצע 2024.
claims.quote: Aleph Farms still has to receive approval for its production line with procedures expected to be completed in the coming few months so that the products will be available for sale by mid-2024.

claims.text: לפי Ynetnews, בראיון מ-2022 העריך טוביה שמוצרי אלף פארמס יגיעו לחנויות ב-2025 או 2026.
claims.quote: In the same interview, Toubia estimated that Aleph Farms products will reach stores in 2025 or 2026.

claims.text: לפי ynet, החברה הישראלית אלף פארמס הודיעה ביום רביעי שקיבלה ממשרד הבריאות אישור רגולטורי ראשון מסוגו.
claims.quote: חברת הפוד-טק הישראלית אלף פארמס (Aleph Farms) הודיעה אתמול (יום ד') כי קיבלה אישור רגולטורי ראשון מסוגו ממשרד הבריאות

claims.text: לפי טוביה, ניתוח טכנו-כלכלי עצמאי צופה עלות ייצור של 6.45 דולר לפאונד ושולי רווח גולמי של 47%, במחיר זהה לבקר רגיל.
claims.quote: This projects a 47% gross margin at price parity with conventional beef, a unit production cost of $6.45 per pound
